users.title: Users
users.naiveServerHint: — Naive is not split per key (server-wide accounting). Mieru is per key.
users.noUsers: No users yet. Click "Add User" to create one.
users.deleteConfirm: Delete user "{{name}}"? This will remove their access immediately.
users.passwordHintEdit: Leave blank to keep current password
users.passwordRequired: Password is required for new users
users.passwordTooShort: Password must be at least 8 characters
users.hy2NotInstalled: Hysteria2 is not installed — install it in Server Settings to issue hy2 keys.
users.emailFedHint: Add an email so this user's configs are pulled from your other (federated) servers into one subscription link.
users.savedRefreshHint: Saved. The list will update in a moment — refresh the page if it looks stale.

config.downloadNote: The user's stored password is embedded automatically. Copy the link or download a config file.
config.mieruPortHint: Leave at the range start unless you want a specific port.
config.mieruPortOutOfRange: Port must be within the Mieru range
config.passwordNote: Enter the user's plain-text password to embed in the config file.
config.qrNote: Scan QR code with client app (iOS: ShadowRocket, Karing)

settings.title: Server Settings
settings.externalDesc: Expose the panel via a TLS subdomain (https://panel.<domain>/<webBasePath>/), protected by basic auth. The panel always stays on 127.0.0.1:3000; Caddy reverse-proxies to it. The root and any path outside webBasePath show a static stub.
settings.externalGenerated: New webBasePath generated — click Apply to save
settings.externalDisableConfirm: Disable external access? The panel will be reachable only via SSH tunnel.
settings.probeSecretDesc: Secret token clients present in headers. Unrecognised clients see the fake site instead.
settings.probeSecretTooShort: Probe secret must be at least 8 characters
settings.probeModeHint: "Bare" matches a known-good reference server. "Secret" requires a special domain to reach the masquerade site.
settings.probeModeUpdated: Probe resistance mode updated — Caddy reloaded
settings.naivePortDesc: Change the HTTPS port for NaiveProxy. Reloads Caddy only — no service restart.
settings.naivePortNote: Changing port will require clients to update their configs.
settings.naiveTuningDesc: Analysis changes nothing. Apply validates the Caddyfile, gracefully reloads only Caddy and rolls back on failure.
settings.tuningHistoryDesc: Recent recommendations and successfully applied changes for all VPN services.
settings.mieruPortDesc: Change the TCP port range for Mieru. Requires full Mieru restart.
settings.mieruPortNote: UFW rules will be updated automatically. Clients must download new configs.
settings.mieruPortConfirm: Changing Mieru ports will restart the Mieru service. Continue?
settings.trafficDesc: Configure Mieru traffic obfuscation pattern and MTU (default 1400).
settings.mieruTuningDesc: Analysis changes nothing. Apply validates the configuration, restarts only Mieru and restores previous settings on failure.
settings.udpDesc: TCP-only is recommended and default. Enable UDP only if your network blocks TCP on Mieru ports. Requires full Mieru restart.
settings.udpNote: UDP mode restarts Mieru. Test TCP first — it works on most networks.
settings.maintenanceDesc: Locks configuration changes without stopping VPN services. Status, diagnostics and encrypted backup remain available.
settings.maintenanceEnabled: Maintenance mode enabled — changes are locked
settings.totpDesc: Add a six-digit authenticator code to administrator login.
settings.totpManual: If scanning is unavailable, enter this secret manually:
settings.totpScan: Scan the QR code and confirm setup with the current code.
settings.totpInvalid: Enter a valid six-digit code and password.
settings.passwordTooShort: New password must be at least 8 characters
settings.backupDesc: Export a full backup (all users + all settings) to a single file, or restore it on a fresh server. If the new server uses the same domain (just point DNS to it), existing client keys keep working with no changes.
settings.backupWarn: New backups are encrypted. Keep the separate passphrase safe: the panel cannot recover it. Legacy plaintext JSON backups can still be imported.
settings.backupBadFile: Not a valid VertaFlux backup file
settings.backupDomainPrompt:
Restore {n} user(s) from backup.

Keep the DOMAIN/ports FROM THE BACKUP ("{d}")?

• OK = keep backup domain (same DNS → existing client keys keep working)
• Cancel = keep THIS server's current domain (clients must download new keys)
settings.backupImportConfirm: This will OVERWRITE the current users and settings with the backup. Continue?
settings.backupUnlockPassphraseLabel: Passphrase for the encrypted backup being restored
settings.backupPassphraseShort: Backup passphrase must contain at least 12 characters
settings.backupUnlockRequired: Enter the backup passphrase before selecting the file
settings.updateCheck_token: A read-only GitHub token is required
settings.author: Author
settings.warpDesc: Routes all of the server's outbound traffic through Cloudflare WARP, hiding the server's real IP. Server-wide mode. Mutually exclusive with the cascade: exactly one of three modes is active — native IP / cascade / WARP.
settings.warpPersist: Add to autostart (bring up after reboot). OFF by default — safer: after a reboot WARP will not come up by itself, so server access is guaranteed.
settings.warpSafeNote: SSH and the panel port are NOT routed into the tunnel — server access is preserved. Only outbound proxy traffic goes through WARP.
settings.warpCascadeLock: Cascade is enabled — disable the cascade first. WARP and cascade cannot be used at the same time.
settings.languageDesc: Select web-panel language. Choice is saved in browser.
settings.cascadeDesc: Relay setup: traffic goes through this server (entry) to the exit server, then to the internet. Mieru uses Variant B (mieru-client + redsocks + iptables) — the provider only sees this (entry) server.
settings.cascadeHy2Hint: ℹ Hysteria2 is cascaded automatically through the same Mieru tunnel (matched by process owner) — no separate Hy2 exit address is needed. Just fill in the Mieru exit below and tick this box.
settings.cascadeNaiveUpstreamHint: Format: https://user:pass@host:port (leave blank to skip Naive cascade)
settings.cascadeMieruHostHint: Address of the exit (EU) node running the same script. Leave blank to skip Mieru cascade.
settings.cascadeNote: When enabled, the relay is configured and started (mieru-client + redsocks + iptables) — this can take up to a minute on first setup.
settings.cascadeStateOff: Cascade is off. Traffic uses the server's normal route.
settings.cascadeStateNaive: Cascade is active for NaiveProxy only.
settings.cascadeStateFull: Cascade is active for NaiveProxy and Mieru.
settings.cascadeStateAttention: Cascade needs attention. Open the technical details.
settings.warpStateOff: WARP is off. The server's normal route is in use.
settings.warpStateAttention: WARP needs attention. Open the technical details.
settings.resetCascadeConfirm: Fully reset the cascade? This clears the config, the Caddy upstream and the mita config (keys are restored), removes iptables/redsocks/watchdog, and restarts the services without the cascade. Egress returns to the native IP.
settings.cascadeReset: Cascade reset — egress returned to the native IP
settings.needKeyFirst: Create at least one key first
settings.cascadeNeedOne: Provide a Naive upstream URL and/or a Mieru exit host
settings.cascadePortRangeInvalid: End port must be ≥ start port
settings.externalStubTitle: Stub page (shown at subdomain root / outside webBasePath)
settings.externalStubDesc: Static HTML served by Caddy at the panel subdomain root and any path outside webBasePath. Separate from the naive fake-site. Edit and save to replace it.
settings.externalStubEmpty: Stub HTML must not be empty
settings.externalBaPassKeep: Basic-auth password (leave blank to keep current)
settings.hy2Desc: Hysteria2 is a fast QUIC/UDP protocol. It runs over UDP and coexists with NaiveProxy on TCP/443. Uses the shared user pool and Caddys certificate (no second email).
settings.hy2NotInstalled: Hysteria2 is not yet installed on this server.
settings.hy2PortHint: Default 443/udp (next to Naive TCP/443). Can be changed to 8443 etc.
settings.hy2PortNote: Changing the port restarts Hy2. Clients must update their links.
settings.hy2InstallConfirm: Install Hysteria2 on this server? May take 1-2 minutes.
settings.hy2ReinstallConfirm: Reinstall Hysteria2? The service will restart.
settings.hy2PortConfirm: Change Hy2 port? The service will restart, clients need new links.
settings.subDomainDesc: Optional dedicated domain for client subscription links (e.g. https://sub.example.com). Leave empty to serve sub-links from the panel domain. Caddy auto-provisions the TLS certificate.
settings.subDomainNote: Point an A-record for this host to this server's IP first, otherwise the TLS certificate cannot be issued.
settings.serverFlagDesc: Optional emoji/text prefix added to the display name of every config this server hands out (e.g. 🇷🇺 or 🇳🇱 RP). Shown in Shadowrocket, Happ, Karing/NekoBox/Throne, etc. Leave empty for no prefix. Bonus links are not touched — put a flag directly into the bonus link if you want one.
settings.fakeSiteDesc: The site shown to anyone who opens the server domain in a browser (camouflage for DPI/probes). Enter a full https:// URL to reverse-proxy a real site, or leave empty to serve the built-in default fake site. Changes rebuild Caddy automatically.
settings.fakeSiteNote: Pick a plausible, always-online site. Leave empty to fall back to the built-in fake site bundled with the panel.
settings.fakeSiteInvalid: Enter a full https:// URL or leave empty

clients.title: Client compatibility
clients.intro: Use the smart subscription when possible. Verification levels distinguish a real tunnel canary from format-only checks.
clients.karingNote: Naive, Mieru and Hy2 were device-tested. VLESS is emitted, but REALITY/XHTTP must be re-tested on the target version.
clients.shadowrocketNote: Naive, Mieru and Hy2 were device-tested. VLESS is emitted, but REALITY/XHTTP must be re-tested on the target version.
clients.singboxNote: Official CLI validates the generated configuration in CI.
clients.familyNote: User-Agent routing and JSON generation are tested; run a connection check on the target device.
clients.xrayNote: Official client is used by the Debian 13 REALITY canary.
clients.mihomoNote: XHTTP transport is covered by an independent tunnel canary.
clients.cliNote: Use for protocol-specific troubleshooting and canary checks.
clients.openfluxNote: Not included in shared users or smart subscriptions.

diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
diagnostics.healthHint: A safe read-only overview. This check does not enable optional protocols.
diagnostics.connectionHint: Checks access policy, identity, DNS/TLS, listener and service state without using or exposing credentials.
diagnostics.connectionReady: Server side is ready; test the current profile on the client device
diagnostics.noProtocols: No managed protocols enabled for this user
diagnostics.networkHint: Public DNS, server IP and certificate identity are checked without changing the server.

toast.naivePortUpdated: NaiveProxy port updated — clients need new configs
toast.mieruPortsUpdated: Mieru ports updated — service restarted, clients need new configs

bonus.title: Bonus links
bonus.hint: Extra links (e.g. vless://) added only to THIS client's subscription. No validation — paste as-is.

onboarding.title: Welcome to VertaFlux
onboarding.welcomeText: NaiveProxy and Mieru are ready. Hysteria2, VLESS and OpenFlux remain opt-in and are never enabled automatically.
onboarding.addressesText: The main domain carries proxy traffic, the panel domain opens administration, and the subscription domain distributes client configurations.
onboarding.securityText: Keep the installation report offline, enable TOTP, create an encrypted backup, then add the first user.

federation.title: Federation
federation.intro: Link several panels so one subscription link delivers configs from multiple servers. Users are matched across servers by their email. This panel pulls configs from the peer nodes you add below and merges them into each user's subscription.
federation.nodeTokenDesc: Give this token to another (main) panel so it can pull this server's configs. Important: this server must have a subscription domain configured (Settings → Subscription Domain) — federation is served there. Keep the token secret. Empty = this server will not answer federation requests.
federation.tokenSetPh: •••••••• (token is set — leave blank to keep)
federation.nodeTokenHint: A token is set. Regenerating replaces it — peers using the old one stop working.
federation.nodeTokenHintSet: A token is set. Generate + Save to replace it (old peers stop working).
federation.nodeTokenHintUnset: No token yet. Generate one and give it to your main panel.
federation.tokenGenerated: Token generated — click Save to apply.
federation.nothingToCopy: Nothing to copy — generate a token first.
federation.nodesDesc: Add each other panel by its SUB-domain (that panel's subscription domain, e.g. https://sub.example.com) and its node token. Federation is served on the sub-domain, next to /sub — the main/fake-site domain will NOT work. Disabled or unreachable peers are silently skipped — a subscription never breaks.
federation.addUrlHint: Use the peer's SUBSCRIPTION domain (Settings → Subscription Domain on that panel), e.g. https://sub.example.com — NOT its main/fake-site domain. Federation is served there next to /sub.
federation.deployConfirm: Deploy user "{{name}}" to all federation nodes? Each node will create (or update) a user with this email and its own local password.
federation.deployNoNodes: No federation nodes to deploy to.
federation.deployNoEmail: This user has no email — federation links users by email. Set an email first.
federation.undeployConfirm: Revoke user "{{name}}" from ALL federation nodes? The user will be removed on every peer (the local user stays).
federation.testConnsHint: Checks each peer for DNS / TLS / token problems without changing anything.
federation.testProbeResistance: node reachable — probe_resistance active (this is normal for a NaiveProxy node; real federation still works)
